findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The display cooler at the front of the store was observed to be stacked past the point of refrigeration. There were many TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) foods that were out of temperature in the cooler. These items include but are not limited to: Peanut Butter & Jelly sandwiches (48-54F), a salad (54F), charcuterie packs (47-54F), buffalo chicken wraps (50-53F), breakfast sandwiches (49F), and Bomb Burritos (46-50F). These items were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. All items discarded were between 46F and 60F. Ensure that this cooler is not over stocked to allow proper refrigeration. Stocking non-TCS items in the corners is highly recommended. Ensure that the temperatures of items in this cooler are frequently checked and avoid over stocking. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.comment:

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Motor oil, antifreeze and other chemicals are stored next to and close to sugar, coffee, and other food or food contact surfaces (like paper towels and cups). Ensure these chemicals are stored in a location to prevent potential contamination of food. Additionally, a barrier can be put between chemicals and food so spilled chemicals cannot contaminate food. The oil and antifreeze were moved over a few inches to avoid possible contamination. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

(B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Creamers and items in the prep cooler are being marked with an improper seven days (10/18-10/25; 10/13-10/20). Think of this rule as the Plus Six Rule and not the seven day rule. Day 1 is the day of creation. Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
[1]  Seven pans/bags of potentially hazardous foods found in pizza prep cooler at temperatures 50 - 55 degrees F (see Voluntary Destruction Form).  CORRECTED - all foods were immediately, voluntarily discarded.  Air thermometer in unit states air at back of cooler is 50 degrees F.  See General Comments for cold-holding recommendations.

[2]  Approximately 20 food items in the lobby end cap display cooler were found at temperatures 48 - 55 degrees F (see Voluntary Destruction Form).  It appears these items were all stored at the edge of the shelf, or in the lower right corner of the cooler.  CORRECTED - all foods were immediately, voluntarily discarded.  Air thermometer in unit states air is 33 degrees F.  Manager may start to use cooler curtain during slow times to protect food.  

Staff should use stem thermometer to frequently check cold-holding temperatures to assure all potentially hazardous foods are held at 41 degrees F or below, or 135 or above for hot foods.

750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:

Opening a lid created great potential for food debris to fall into stocked food within pan.  CORRECTED - manager had staff take a part and thoroughly detail clean all parts of prep cooler.  Make sure to clean food debris spills as they occur, to protect food when prep pans are open.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Two wet wiping cloths were observed balled up on left end of 3-pan sink.  Wiping cloths should be stored within a sanitizer bucket, clean and dry, or in soiled laundry.  If cloths are wet, and soiled, and staff wishes to hang them to dry, consider hanging them along edge of soiled laundry basket, which is located in back room, and far from food prep and dish sanitizing areas.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The interior of the ice cream freezer is soiled, especially around top rim, which has caught food debris, dirt and dust.  Clean this freezer (and make sure to defrost regularly).
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The floor under the far west end of the soda fountain is soiled (from pizza kitchen-side).  Clean and maintain this floor.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Five bottles of concentrated cleaners and sanitizers were found stored on the vegetable prep surface adjacent to vegetable wash sink.  CORRECTED - bottles were immediately moved to shelf under hand sink.  Vegetable prep sink should be kept clean and clear of chemicals.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloth found on counter top next to lobby/coffee station hand sink.  CORRECTED - cloth was immediately placed on side of 3-pan sink to dry.  Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer bucket when not in use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces are soiled:
(a) walk-in cooler fans (accumulated dust and debris) (REPEAT), 
(b) metal shelf under backside of soda fountain (cups, debris, dirt), 
(c) cabinet under lobby/coffee station hand sink, 
(d) all interior surfaces of cooler under lobby hot-holding rollers (CORRECTED).
Clean and maintain these surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Upon start of inspection, hand sink had two bags resting in the sink basin.  CORRECTED - bags were immediately removed.  Sinks must never be blocked by any items at any time.  They should not be used for any purpose other than hand washing.
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors are soiled:
(a) under gallons of tea in walk-in cooler, 
(b) behind soda syrup boxes closest to walk-in cooler, 
(c) corner next to walk-in cooler by mouse trap (old blue mouse droppings), 
(d) under the other two soda syrup stacks (back room), 
(e) under soda fountain (back room), 
(f) to left of soda fountain (back room), 
(g) floor under car wash chemicals (soap/conditioner spills).
Clean and maintain these floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
The following walls and attached equipment are soiled:
(a) wall behind car wash chemicals (streaks of soap/conditioner), 
(b) door jam around car wash door (rusted), 
(c) car wash door (along bottom - rust).
Clean and replace or re-surface the aforementioned items.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
